review.headline: A Pirc where pressure and a passed b-pawn carried you, until the clock ended it

sections.text: You met the Pirc with 2.d4 and 3.Nf3 and the standard setup 4.Be2, 5.Nbd2 and 6.O-O. Against 7...b5 you played 8.e5, a good central push, and after 8...dxe5 9.dxe5 Nd5 the engine had you at +1.7.
Black's 11...Bg4 was a mistake and you kept the edge. 12.g3 was not the engine's choice (12.h3 was), but 13.cxb5 and 14.bxa6 won pawns and 16.Nxf3! was the right recapture after 15...Bxf3.

18.Nd4?? was the big error. It left a piece to be won and dropped you from +2.9 to -4.2; 18.Bc4 was better. But Black replied 18...Nxd4 19.Qxc5 and then 19...Ne6?, missing 19...Nf3+, which would have forked your king and rook.
From there you rebuilt: 23...Rxc1 24.Raxc1 and queen trades with 26.gxh4 left a far better endgame. The b-pawn advanced from 32.b4 to 39.b7, and despite 40.Rd8?? you won, with Black out of time.

review.turning_point: 18.Nd4 gave up a piece, but Black missed 19...Nf3+ and handed the game back.
review.focus: 18.Nd4 was a lapse of piece safety. Check whether every piece you move leaves something undefended; 18.Bc4 was safe and kept you better.
